jobs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Reference image: the attached current in-game Amy sprite, identity and pixel-art reference. Each cell has exactly one complete Amy, facing RIGHT, same pixel-art rendering and scale, pink quills, red headband, large green eye, cream face, red dress, white gloves and red boots from the reference. Preserve recognizability, no weapons. Crisp simple pixel-art suitable for a 50-pixel-wide game character, no painted glow. Character entirely inside each cell, clear transparent gutter on all sides. Same head/body size and consistent pivot at cell center bottom 90 percent. ROW ONE, left to right: 3 jump launch poses: slight crouch, strong push off, body extending upward. ROW TWO: 3 aerial ascent/apex poses: arms drawn back, rising with knees bent, relaxed apex. ROW THREE: 3 falling poses: beginning descent, falling arms open, legs bracing. ROW FOUR: 3 landing recovery poses: soft knee compression, half recovery, upright idle. Feet baseline same 90 percent in all frames, animate the body/legs around this anchor rather than moving the sprite through the cell. Every pose is distinct but restrained enough for smooth animation. Equal mathematically aligned 3 by 4 grid, no border lines, no titles, no labels, no numbers, NO platform/background/particles. Twelve characters only, one per cell, no detached hands or extra limbs. True transparent alpha.

jobs.knee_correction_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the full twelve-frame 3-column by 4-row Amy pixel-art sprite sheet in image 1. Image 2 is an ERROR REFERENCE crop supplied by the user: do not copy its white background or its distorted knees. Correct the leg anatomy and knee readability in the full sheet, especially ascent row 2 and falling row 3. Keep the exact character identity, face, head, dress, palette, gloves, pixel-art style, frame order, twelve poses and genuine transparency. Every visible leg must read as one short pink thigh from hip, ONE clearly positioned pink knee, one pink lower leg entering a red boot at the white boot cuff. The red boot is footwear, not an extra joint. No double knees, no U shaped rubber legs, no boots joined directly to hips, no bent boot shafts, no disconnected pink blobs. Keep the far leg partly hidden behind the near leg where useful instead of tangling them. Three falling poses: extend legs gradually downward from hips, knees slightly bent, red boots hanging down naturally; last falling pose has BOTH feet directed downward for landing, NEVER one straight horizontal leg with a backwards knee. Landing row 4: knees flex slightly forward while rigid boots remain on same horizontal baseline, then straighten. Maintain a compact readable silhouette at small pixel size. Each of the 12 sprites centered in its own equal square cell, complete feet inside each cell with margin, common feet baseline around 90 percent height; no pose touches its neighbor. No grid lines or text. Transparent background, no floor, no effects. Focus exclusively on coherent hips-knees-ankles and retain all upper-body artwork as closely as possible.
jobs.revision_rodillas_y_pies_v2:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: image 1, current twelve-frame Amy sprite sheet. The knee and foot drawings in it ARE WRONG and must be REPLACED, not traced.
Primary request: completely redraw ALL legs and boots below the skirt in EVERY cell, while preserving upper bodies, faces, dresses, character identity, pixel art palette, 3 columns x 4 rows, twelve poses, transparent gutters and true alpha.
LOWER BODY CONSTRUCTION: exactly TWO slender pink legs attached to two separate hips under the skirt. Show a visible pink thigh, ONE knee, and a visible pink calf entering a white boot cuff. Make the pink legs longer than in the bad reference, enough to clearly see the knee ABOVE the cuff. One joint per knee; no pink spheres at the skirt hem pretending to be knees. The far leg can overlap partly but its separate boot must still read clearly.
FOOTWEAR: exactly TWO matching RED BOOTS per character, each with one WHITE cuff near the top and a GREY flat sole at the bottom. Each boot has a short RIGID upright shaft, a small heel at LEFT, ankle over heel, and a distinct toe projecting RIGHT. Amy faces RIGHT, so both boot toes point RIGHT, not toward left or into each other. Boot shafts NEVER bend into C/U shapes. Knees are pink anatomy above the white cuffs, never a bend in a red boot. Give the toes length and the boots a solid foot silhouette, not red teardrops or limp mittens.
POSES: Row 1 slight knee bend, push-off, straight takeoff. Row 2 rising: one knee modestly forward, other leg trailing gently; both boot shapes remain rigid and toes RIGHT; do not fold legs tightly under skirt. Row 3 falling: progressively extend both legs DOWN with gentle knee flexion, both feet BELOW hips, toes right. Last falling pose has two distinct feet preparing to land. Row 4 soft landing compression then recovery then upright stance, both flat soles level in each frame. Shallow readable poses are better than extreme contortions.
Keep all twelve full characters in their existing cells, with generous empty lanes, at least 10 percent transparent margin all around each sprite. No sprite crosses a cell boundary. Preserve similar scale but make room for clear pink calves. A naturally proportioned stylized cartoon anatomy, NOT photorealism.
No labels, no numbers, no background, no grid lines, no added objects or effects. Do not merely add a pink blob to existing malformed boots: erase and redraw the lower limbs coherently.
